messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: GeoDNS health anomaly detected for eu namespace — elevated resolver error rate (SERVFAIL ~>40%) and Cloudflare edge 5xx spike. Automated Route53 failover triggered for some records. Paging oncall-sre.

sarah: ack, I'm oncall. grabbing context and will triage.

sarah: initial impact summary — external API endpoints in eu region returning 502/503 for some customers. Observed routing: some clients hit Cloudflare edges that are returning 5xx, others are failing at DNS resolution (SERVFAIL).

jia: digging in — running some queries against public resolvers and our authoritative.

jia: ```
$ dig @1.1.1.1 api.eu.example.com A
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 0, ADDITIONAL: 1
```

jia: ```
$ dig @8.8.8.8 api.eu.example.com A +tcp
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 67890
;; ANSWER SECTION:
api.eu.example.com. 300 IN A 52.14.22.11
```

jia: looks like some resolvers are failing over UDP but succeed over TCP. could be EDNS0/UDP MTU fragmentation or middlebox dropping UDP.

mike: I'm seeing intermittent packet drops to the Cloudflare EU edge from our peering — mtr shows ~20% loss at hop 7 for a subset of probes.

samir: created tickets: Cloudflare ticket #CF-123456 (edge 84 errors + UDP fallback), AWS Route53 ticket #AWS-654321 (health check flapping). Adding debug dumps to both.

sarah: short mitigation proposals: 1) temporarily set GeoDNS to prefer Route53-only policies for eu A records to avoid CF edge instability; 2) reduce TTLs to 60 where we can to accelerate rollouts; 3) for critical enterprise tenants, create CNAME overrides to us-east fallback. Thoughts?

jia: agree on preference change, but note TTL reductions won't fully propagate instantly — many resolvers honor previous TTL until expiry. still worth doing for new queries. Also ask CF about forcing TCP fallback or enabling alternative port.

mike: deployment-wise I can flip geo policy to prefer route53 for the eu pool now. I'll stage the change and monitor for DNS query success/failure.

samir: making the policy change now. Will comment when complete.

samir: policy switch applied -> preferring Route53 for eu records. lowering authoritative TTL from 300 -> 60 (request submitted, will take effect at authoritative zone immediately).

jia: monitoring results: after policy switch many previously-servfail clients now resolve to us-east addresses. Error rate dropped from 42% -> 9% in 3m window. Good partial mitigation.

sarah: updating incident severity to sev2. Notifying CS to reach out to impacted customers and record SLO breaches.

cs-team: notified top-20 impacted customers via email and opened incident call with two enterprise customers — CS will coordinate any credits or remediation calls.

incident-bot: Reminder: please attach runbook tag "dns-geo-failover" and link this thread to incident board.

elaine: quick ops note: even though preferring Route53 helps, some resolvers still show intermittent SERVFAIL for ~2m intervals. Might be resolver-side caching of old negative responses. We should ask CF/AWS to check their authoritative DNS stacks too.

jia: added diagnostic: many failing resolvers return SERVFAIL on UDP but respond on TCP. That strongly suggests UDP path issues/fragmentation. Already included tcp fallback note in CF ticket. Also posted PCAP snippet to ticket.

mike: handoff — I'll be the primary overnight. actions taken: 1) geo policy switched to route53-prefer, 2) TTL lowered to 60, 3) CF support ticket opened + debug attached, 4) Route53 ticket open and health checks being reviewed, 5) CS notified. Monitoring dashboards show requests/second and error rate.

sarah: thanks — leaving detailed notes in the incident board and will sync on postmortem tomorrow. mike, if you escalate to CF/AWS engineering, call me.

mike: ack. I'll keep watch and post updates every 30m or on status change. Handoff complete.

incident-bot: Note: please remember to include "customer-impact" section in the postmortem and attach the list of impacted tenant ids.

mike: quick customer impact tally: ~17 customers saw errors, 2 enterprise customers had pagebreaks and opened support tickets. Estimated duration of elevated errors ~18 minutes before mitigation reduced errors; total service degradation window ~45 minutes including partial flapping. CS already scheduled follow-ups.

jia: followup item for postmortem: evaluate forcing TCP or split-path mitigations, consider adding UDP-size/EDNS probes to our active healthchecks, and add a step in runbook to coordinate TTL changes earlier in future.

elaine: also suggest a dashboard alert rule for UDP vs TCP discrepancy per resolver to catch similar patterns earlier.

mike: will create a tracking ticket for the runbook updates and the postmortem. closing handoff — monitoring in steady state for now.

sarah: closing note: thank you team. we'll do a full write-up and action list in the incident tracker. :white_check_mark:
